A system and method are provided for controlling communications on a mobile platform that includes multiple platform applications. The platform has a communications system arranged to send data received from one or more of the platform applications and to carry out wireless data transmission using one of several supported communication links. The system also includes a data management module.

The system and method are configured to obtain performance information representing the presently available bandwidth of each communication link assigned to, or associated with, the platform applications. For each platform application, the system determines the data that is to be sent to a recipient node and compares the bandwidth needed for that data with the currently available bandwidth of the corresponding communication link assigned to, or associated with, that application.

If the comparison shows that the available bandwidth of a communication link is not adequate for the bandwidth required by a particular platform application, the system creates information data and sends it to that particular platform application, or to a quality-of-service interface linked to it. When the information data is received, the platform application, or its associated quality-of-service interface, modifies at least one parameter of its application data so that it matches the currently available bandwidth of its respective communication link before transmission to the recipient node.
outputs.L3:
The method manages communications for a moving platform that includes multiple platform applications, each capable of using one or more supported wireless communication links. These communication links may vary in performance over time as the platform moves, and the method is designed to ensure that data transmissions are adjusted according to the current communication conditions.

The system receives performance data for the wireless communication links associated with the platform applications. This performance data indicates, among other things, the current available bandwidth of each communication link. Because the available bandwidth may change dynamically, the system monitors or obtains this information to determine whether each communication link can support the data that the corresponding platform application intends to transmit.

For each platform application, the system identifies the data that is to be transmitted over a relevant communication link. The system then determines the bandwidth requirement of that data and compares the requirement with the current available bandwidth of the corresponding communication link. This comparison allows the system to determine whether the data can be transmitted in its current form without exceeding the bandwidth capacity of the link.

If the system determines that the available bandwidth of a communication link is insufficient for a specified platform application, the system generates information data related to the bandwidth condition. This information data is sent to the specified platform application or to a quality of service interface associated with that application. The information data may indicate that the bandwidth is limited, identify the available bandwidth, or otherwise provide guidance for adapting the data to be transmitted.

In response, the platform application or the associated quality of service interface adapts at least one parameter of the data before transmission so that the data better matches the current available bandwidth of the communication link. For example, the application or interface may reduce a data rate, lower a resolution, compress the data, delay nonessential data, or otherwise modify the transmission characteristics. As a result, the data transmitted by the platform application is adjusted to the available communication resources, improving the reliability and efficiency of communications for the moving platform.
outputs.L4:
A communications management method for a moving platform, such as an aircraft, train, ship, vehicle, or unmanned system, manages data transmissions over a plurality of wireless communication links whose available bandwidth may vary over time. The platform may include several applications that exchange data with remote systems, including voice, video, telemetry, navigation, maintenance, passenger connectivity, command-and-control, or operational data services. Because the moving platform may travel through different coverage areas, experience changing signal quality, or switch between different communication networks, the bandwidth available to each application may increase or decrease during operation.

The method monitors the bandwidth that is currently available on one or more wireless links associated with the platform. These links may include, for example, satellite communication links, cellular links, air-to-ground links, Wi-Fi links, radio links, or other wireless communication channels. A communications manager, network controller, or similar bandwidth management component determines the capacity available on each link and may also determine how much of that capacity has been allocated to individual platform applications. The monitoring may be performed continuously, periodically, or in response to a detected change in link condition, network congestion, handoff, link failure, or priority change.

For each application, the communications manager identifies the application’s transmission requirements. These requirements may include a requested data rate, minimum bandwidth, latency limit, packet loss tolerance, priority level, quality-of-service requirement, media resolution, sampling rate, update rate, or other parameter that affects the amount of bandwidth needed for the application to operate as intended. The communications manager compares those requirements with the amount of link capacity currently allocated to the application. If the allocated capacity is sufficient, the application may continue transmitting normally. If the allocated capacity is not sufficient, the communications manager determines that the application’s current transmission configuration exceeds the available bandwidth.

When insufficient bandwidth is detected, the communications manager provides a notification to the affected application, to a quality-of-service interface associated with the application, or to another control component responsible for adapting the application’s communications behavior. The notification may indicate the amount of bandwidth currently available, the amount of bandwidth allocated to the application, the degree of shortfall, the link being used, a recommended data rate, or a change in quality-of-service status. In some implementations, the notification may be sent through an application programming interface, middleware layer, network management interface, or operating system service.

In response to the notification, the application adjusts one or more parameters of the data it transmits so that its communication requirements better match the current link conditions. For example, a video application may reduce image resolution, frame rate, compression quality, or bit rate. A telemetry application may reduce its reporting frequency, aggregate data before transmission, or prioritize only essential parameters. A voice or audio application may select a lower-bit-rate codec. A file transfer application may delay nonessential transfers, reduce transmission rate, or pause until additional bandwidth becomes available. Other applications may compress data, discard noncritical information, change update intervals, or modify their quality-of-service level.

By allowing the application to adapt its data transmission behavior based on current bandwidth availability, the method reduces congestion, packet loss, retransmissions, delay, and inefficient use of limited wireless resources. Rather than continuing to transmit at a rate that exceeds the capacity of the link, the application is informed of the limitation and can alter its output accordingly. This enables more reliable communication for high-priority services and allows multiple applications on the moving platform to share available bandwidth more effectively.

The method is particularly useful in environments where connectivity changes frequently and unpredictably. As the moving platform travels, it may transition between communication coverage zones, experience interference, encounter weather-related degradation, or use links having different capacities and costs. The communications manager can respond to these changes by updating bandwidth allocations and notifying applications when their transmission requirements no longer fit the available capacity. When bandwidth later improves, the communications manager may similarly notify applications that additional capacity is available, allowing them to increase data quality, restore higher update rates, or resume deferred transmissions.

In this manner, the communications management method provides a dynamic feedback mechanism between the platform’s communication links and the applications that use them. By monitoring link bandwidth, comparing application requirements with allocated capacity, and causing applications to adapt their transmitted data, the method improves efficiency, reliability, and quality of service for communications to and from a moving platform under changing wireless network conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a European patent-style description of an invention involving platform applications, communication links, a data management module, and dynamic adjustment of application data when bandwidth is insufficient.
counterfactuals.output:
**Description**

**Technical Field**

The present invention relates to the management of data exchange between software applications executing on a platform and remote or local communication endpoints. More particularly, the invention relates to a platform comprising a plurality of platform applications, one or more communication links, and a data management module configured to dynamically adjust application data to be transmitted when available bandwidth is insufficient.

**Background**

Modern computing platforms, such as vehicle platforms, industrial control systems, mobile devices, edge computing nodes, and distributed sensor platforms, often execute a plurality of applications that exchange data with external systems. Such data may include sensor data, telemetry, status information, control information, media data, diagnostic data, or user-related data.

The data exchange may take place over one or more communication links. These links may differ in bandwidth, latency, reliability, cost, or availability. Examples include cellular links, satellite links, wireless local area network links, wired Ethernet links, vehicle-to-everything links, and short-range radio links.

In practice, the bandwidth available on a communication link may vary over time. Bandwidth may become insufficient due to network congestion, weak signal strength, handover events, interference, subscription limits, or competing data flows. If applications continue to transmit data without adaptation, data packets may be delayed, dropped, or transmitted at excessive cost. This may impair the operation of the platform, particularly where some application data is more time-critical or safety-relevant than other data.

Known approaches may throttle communication globally or may allow individual applications to react independently to communication constraints. However, such approaches may be inefficient because the applications may not have a complete view of communication link conditions, platform-wide priorities, or data dependencies.

There is therefore a need for an improved mechanism for managing application data in a platform when available bandwidth is insufficient.

**Summary**

According to an aspect, a platform is provided comprising a plurality of platform applications, at least one communication link, and a data management module. The platform applications are configured to generate application data for transmission via the at least one communication link. The data management module is configured to determine a bandwidth requirement associated with the application data and to determine an available bandwidth of the at least one communication link. If the available bandwidth is insufficient for transmitting the application data in its original form, the data management module dynamically adjusts the application data before transmission.

The dynamic adjustment may comprise reducing a data rate, reducing a sampling frequency, reducing a resolution, compressing data, selecting a subset of data elements, aggregating data, changing a transmission interval, delaying transmission, suppressing non-critical data, prioritising critical data, or converting the application data into an alternative representation requiring less bandwidth.

The data management module may be implemented as middleware, as a platform service, as part of an operating system, as part of a communication stack, or as a distributed module comprising components executed in different parts of the platform.

By providing a data management module that centrally or semi-centrally evaluates bandwidth availability and adapts application data accordingly, the platform can maintain communication of higher-priority information while reducing or deferring lower-priority information when bandwidth is constrained.

**Detailed Description of Embodiments**

A platform according to an embodiment comprises a processing arrangement configured to execute a plurality of platform applications. The platform may be, for example, a vehicle computing platform, a robotic platform, a medical monitoring platform, a mobile computing platform, a smart infrastructure platform, or an industrial automation platform.

The plurality of platform applications may include applications having different communication requirements. For example, a first application may generate status data at frequent intervals, a second application may generate sensor data, a third application may generate diagnostic data, and a fourth application may generate multimedia data. The applications may provide their data to a data management module for transmission via one or more communication links.

The communication links may include a first communication link and a second communication link. The first communication link may have a relatively high bandwidth but variable availability, such as a cellular communication link. The second communication link may have a lower bandwidth but greater reliability, such as a narrowband radio link. In other embodiments, only one communication link is provided.

The data management module may be configured to receive, intercept, monitor, or otherwise obtain application data generated by the platform applications. The data management module may further obtain metadata associated with the application data. The metadata may include at least one of:

- an application identifier;
- a data type;
- a priority level;
- a required latency;
- a maximum permitted age of the data;
- a minimum required transmission rate;
- a preferred communication link;
- a security requirement;
- a compression capability;
- a permitted degradation level;
- a dependency on other data;
- a safety or operational relevance classification.

In an embodiment, the data management module determines a bandwidth requirement of application data generated by one or more platform applications. The bandwidth requirement may be determined based on the size of the data, the generation frequency, a requested transmission period, a data encoding format, or historical transmission behaviour.

The data management module also determines available bandwidth of at least one communication link. Available bandwidth may be determined by measurements, by feedback from a modem or network interface, by link quality indicators, by acknowledgement timing, by packet loss, by information received from a network, or by prediction based on historical data.

If the available bandwidth is sufficient, the data management module may allow the application data to be transmitted without adjustment or with only standard processing such as packetisation or encryption.

If the available bandwidth is insufficient, the data management module dynamically adjusts the application data. The adjustment is performed dynamically in that it is responsive to current or predicted bandwidth conditions and may change over time while the platform remains in operation.

In one embodiment, the data management module applies a priority-based adjustment. Application data having a high priority is transmitted with little or no degradation, while application data having a lower priority is reduced, delayed, compressed, aggregated, or suppressed. For example, emergency status data may be transmitted immediately, whereas non-critical log data may be buffered for later transmission.

In another embodiment, the data management module applies data-rate reduction. If a platform application generates sensor values at a first sampling frequency, the data management module may transmit only every nth sample or may instruct the platform application to generate data at a lower sampling frequency. The value of n may be adjusted according to the available bandwidth.

In another embodiment, the data management module applies resolution reduction. For example, image data, video data, map data, environmental data, or measurement data may be converted from a higher resolution to a lower resolution before transmission. In the case of image data, the adjustment may include reducing the image size, reducing colour depth, increasing compression, reducing frame rate, or transmitting only selected regions of interest.

In another embodiment, the data management module aggregates data. Instead of transmitting individual data messages, the module may combine multiple data values into a summary message. For example, a sequence of temperature measurements may be replaced by a minimum value, a maximum value, an average value, and a time period.

In another embodiment, the data management module selects an alternative encoding format. The alternative encoding format may be a lossy or lossless compressed format, a binary representation instead of a textual representation, or a compact representation containing only changes relative to previously transmitted data.

In another embodiment, the data management module delays transmission of selected data. The delayed data may be stored in a buffer or memory and transmitted when sufficient bandwidth becomes available. The module may discard buffered data if the data exceeds a maximum age or if newer data renders the buffered data obsolete.

The data management module may be configured to generate control instructions for one or more platform applications. The control instructions may instruct an application to reduce a data generation rate, modify a data format, reduce a measurement resolution, disable a non-essential data stream, or provide only data matching specified criteria. Thus, adjustment may be performed either within the data management module after data generation or within the application before data generation.

The data management module may maintain a policy database. The policy database may define rules for adjusting different classes of application data. A policy may specify, for example, that safety-critical data is not to be suppressed, that diagnostic data may be delayed for a predetermined period, and that multimedia data may be compressed or reduced in frame rate when bandwidth is limited.

The policies may be preconfigured, updated remotely, learned from previous operating conditions, or selected according to an operating mode of the platform. For example, a vehicle platform may use a first policy during normal operation, a second policy during an emergency event, and a third policy during maintenance.

In an embodiment, the data management module determines a degree of insufficiency between required bandwidth and available bandwidth. The adjustment may then be selected in accordance with the degree of insufficiency. For a minor insufficiency, the module may apply compression only. For a greater insufficiency, the module may additionally reduce sampling rates or suppress low-priority data. For a severe insufficiency, the module may transmit only essential data.

The platform may comprise a link selection module or the data management module may perform link selection. If multiple communication links are available, the module may allocate application data to different communication links according to bandwidth, cost, latency, reliability, or priority. If no single link has sufficient bandwidth, the module may divide adjusted or unadjusted data across multiple links.

In an embodiment, the data management module predicts future bandwidth availability. Prediction may be based on movement of the platform, signal history, network information, time of day, geographical position, or known communication coverage maps. The module may pre-emptively reduce data generation or pre-buffer data when a reduction in bandwidth is expected.

The data management module may also monitor the effect of adjustment. If bandwidth improves, the module may restore higher data rates, higher resolution, less compression, or previously suppressed data streams. Thus, the adjustment may be reversible and continuously adaptable.

In an embodiment, the module assigns each data stream an adaptation level selected from a plurality of adaptation levels. A first adaptation level may correspond to full fidelity. A second adaptation level may correspond to compressed data. A third adaptation level may correspond to reduced frequency. A fourth adaptation level may correspond to summary-only transmission. A fifth adaptation level may correspond to suppression or buffering. The adaptation level may be selected based on available bandwidth and priority.

The invention may be implemented in software, hardware, or a combination thereof. A computer program may comprise instructions which, when executed by one or more processors of the platform, cause the platform to perform the functions of the data management module. The computer program may be stored on a computer-readable medium.

**Example Operation**

In an example, a platform executes three platform applications. A first platform application generates operational state data at 10 kbit/s, a second platform application generates sensor data at 500 kbit/s, and a third platform application generates diagnostic log data at 100 kbit/s. The total bandwidth requirement is therefore 610 kbit/s.

The data management module determines that a communication link currently provides only 300 kbit/s of available bandwidth. The module determines that the operational state data has high priority, the sensor data has medium priority, and the diagnostic log data has low priority.

The module transmits the operational state data without reduction. The module reduces the sensor data by lowering the sampling rate and applying compression, thereby reducing the bandwidth requirement to 250 kbit/s. The module buffers the diagnostic log data for later transmission. The total bandwidth requirement is thereby reduced to a level compatible with the available bandwidth.

When the communication link later provides 1 Mbit/s of available bandwidth, the data management module restores the original sampling rate of the sensor data and transmits at least part of the buffered diagnostic log data.

**Advantages**

Embodiments of the invention may provide one or more of the following advantages:

- improved utilisation of variable-bandwidth communication links;
- reduced packet loss and transmission delay;
- continued transmission of high-priority data during bandwidth limitations;
- centralised or coordinated adaptation across multiple applications;
- reduced need for each application to implement its own bandwidth adaptation logic;
- improved robustness of platforms operating in changing network environments;
- ability to degrade data quality gracefully rather than interrupting communication entirely.

The features disclosed in the foregoing description may be provided independently or in any technically feasible combination. The scope of protection is not limited by the examples described above, which are provided for illustrative purposes.
